title: How the build's sessions are organized: a coordinator per repo
why: Orchestrator, Oct 28 14:58 CDT: you proposed three tiers (coordinator, lane leads, triage, all Opus); an Opus blind review with web research says the shape is sound but the cut is wrong.
note: Ruling, Oct 28 14:59 CDT (shiv, chat, first part): one coordinator per repo; coordinators may message each other to share a resource (a simulator, a loaded machine); a coordinator may touch another repo when needed, but its main job is its own repo's lanes; claude-settings is a special case that touches every repo a little. Ruling, Oct 28 15:03 CDT (shiv, chat): triage is always a standing session, never on demand, and each coordinator spawns it first, before any lane session. Still open, waiting-page item 50 (pick a recommended): lane sessions on Sonnet or Opus. The review: one coordinator per repo, not one for all repos, since batches, CI and the question page are per repo. Triage becomes a planner the coordinator starts on demand and stays the only roadmap writer; the coordinator owns the repo's question page, so shiv faces one writer. Lane sessions run Sonnet, build themselves and spawn a fresh reviewer; Opus only on round 3 or the coordinator's flag (Anthropic's gain came from an Opus lead over Sonnet workers). Ruling, Oct 28 15:01 CDT (shiv, via the coordinator): no coded guard and no file-ownership record for lanes that clash on shared files; a good brief is enough and orchestrators merge overlapping edits in different parts of one file. His want instead: better file splitting, so lanes touch different files (no lane filed yet). False done is already covered: merge.py reads the head and CI from GitHub and stops on a moved head, and rule verification-verify-against-repo applies; no new work. One name for the coordinator in GLOSSARY.md, retiring orchestrator, point guard (degen) and arbiter (q_max). Sources: Anthropic's multi-agent research system, Building effective agents, Claude Code subagents and agent-teams docs, Cognition's two multi-agent posts. No build until shiv answers. Port: yes, every repo with standing roles. Placed after c200 (triage 12, Oct 28). Task, Oct 28 15:04 CDT (shiv, via the coordinator): revise the solo-versus-orchestrate rules in claude-settings to match the tiers (coordinator, standing triage spawned first, lane sessions as their own orchestrators). He wants an Opus review on building it out and is open to being interviewed. An Opus plan agent is drafting the change list and owner questions; the coordinator sends the questions to triage for the waiting page. Two more questions from shiv, Oct 28 15:10 CDT, for the planner review (coordinator relays): should he answer triage directly more often, to save both sessions' context; is a third standing role needed beside coordinator and triage. Also a per-tier context limit, Oct 28 15:08 CDT: can orchestrators on Opus 5.5 have a different context limit than the coordinator (docs research pending; waiting-page item to follow).
